title: What kind of triangle has these three angles?
description: Each set of angles is first checked to add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. The biggest angle then names the kind of triangle. Keeko's doubt is that a triangle with an obtuse angle has no acute angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: the biggest angle names the kind of triangle, and every triangle has at least two acute angles. Watch for students who think an obtuse triangle has no acute angle.

source: A classification of triangles based on their angle measures is acute-angled, right-angled and obtuse-angled triangles. We have already seen what a right-angled triangle is. It is a triangle with one right angle. Similarly, an obtuse-angled triangle has one obtuse angle. What could an acute-angled triangle be? Can we define it as a triangle with one acute angle? Why not? In an acute-angled triangle, all three angles are acute angles.
video_script.why: The child knows that the three angles of a triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees and now names a triangle from its angles.
video_script.anchor: three triangles with their angles marked in degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: an obtuse angled triangle has no acute angle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko looks at the triangle with one hundred and twenty degrees and says it has no acute angle, but the other two angles must share the sixty degrees that are left, so both are acute.
video_script.payoff_line: They are acute angled, right angled and obtuse angled

final_answer.value: (a) acute-angled (b) right-angled (c) obtuse-angled; all three have an acute angle
final_answer.spoken: they are acute angled, right angled and obtuse angled, and all three have an acute angle

maths_rules: the biggest angle names the kind: 70° is less than 90°, 90° is a right angle, 120° is more than 90°
all three angles acute: acute-angled; one right angle: right-angled; one obtuse angle: obtuse-angled
every triangle here has an acute angle: three, two and two

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the three angles of a triangle must add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Fifty plus sixty plus seventy is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Ninety plus fifty plus forty is one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>One hundred and twenty plus thirty plus thirty is one hundred and eighty. All three triangles exist.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>They are acute angled, right angled and obtuse angled.
<bookmark mark='acute'/>A triangle with all three angles acute is called acute angled.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The second has one right angle, so it is right angled.
<bookmark mark='obtuse'/>A triangle with one obtuse angle is called obtuse angled.
<bookmark mark='all'/>All three triangles have at least one acute angle.
